title: Geopolitical Daily
email_subject: Oil Tops $100 as Iran-US Fight Escalates
preheader: Biggest wave of Gulf ship attacks yet, plus Germany's far-right earthquake.
intro_text: Good morning. It's Thursday, September 10, 2026 — the 3 stories that matter most today, plus 8 quick updates from around the world.

stories.story_title: Iran and US Trade Biggest Wave of Attacks Yet on Gulf Shipping
stories.why_important: Iran says it hit 10 ships near the Strait of Hormuz after the US sank five Iranian tankers. Brent crude broke $100 a barrel for the first time since July. This is the biggest tit-for-tat shipping attack since the war began six months ago, and it puts a critical oil route at real risk.
stories.what_overlooked: Much of the ship and casualty count comes from Iran's own military, with little independent confirmation of the damage claimed.
stories.prediction: Watch for oil prices to keep rising and shippers to start avoiding the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.story_title: Far-Right AfD's Landslide Win Rattles Germany and Europe
stories.why_important: The AfD nearly doubled its 2021 result to take 43.8% in Saxony-Anhalt. The win pressures Chancellor Merz and could push Berlin toward a softer line on China and looser EU ties.
stories.what_overlooked: Coverage dwells on shockwaves in Berlin and Paris but says little about the economic grievances driving voters to the AfD.
stories.prediction: Watch for Merz's coalition to debate migration and China policy within days.

stories.story_title: Trump Promises $5,000 Checks to Every American If GOP Wins Midterms
stories.why_important: Trump pledged a $5,000 payment to every US adult, a plan that would cost roughly $1.35 trillion. It's unclear how he would pay for it or whether it is even legal.
stories.what_overlooked: No outlet explains where the money would come from or whether Congress would ever approve such a payout.
stories.prediction: Watch for economists and lawmakers to challenge the plan's cost and legality this week.

quick_hits.text: A ferry fire off Palawan killed 5 people and left more than 80 missing, Philippine Coast Guard said.
Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon quit, saying AI could kill all humans and both his former employers are 'gambling with our lives.'
Copernicus says August was the joint-hottest month on record, with temperatures 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels.
Russia and Vietnam signed 17 deals, including a strategic oil reserve pact, during President To Lam's Moscow visit.
Zelensky's plane was delayed leaving Moldova after Norway's PM said it nearly collided with a drone.
Syria condemned Netanyahu's visit to Israeli troops on Mount Hermon in Syrian territory as an illegal incursion.
Houthi rebels say Saudi forces launched 54 air raids in 12 hours, killing three children, as Yemen's war deepens.
Macron called on Europe to build its own crewed spaceflight program within a decade.

big_number.context: The estimated cost of Trump's promised $5,000 payment to every US adult if Republicans win the midterms.
